title: Function-vector routing from context
hypothesis: A context-derived Mirror router selects a stored function-vector code with >=95% accuracy and retains downstream task utility within 5pp of oracle task-ID routing, with less actual payload than per-task vectors plus explicit IDs.
physical_object: one frozen GPT-2 and a bank of 16 task function vectors
mirror_coordinate: content-derived context address selecting one stored FV; separate router and execution errors
logical_multiplicity: 16 procedure x token-domain functions selected without an external task ID

development.allowed: tokenization and code sanity; fixed block 6 and cosine routing, no fresh-informed tuning

success_gate: Direct ICL exceeds 12.5% in every fresh world; routed identity accuracy >=95%; routed target accuracy within 5 percentage points of oracle; router+FV bytes below explicit per-task vectors plus IDs.
failure_gate: Direct ICL valid and routed accuracy <95%, or routed target quality >5pp below oracle, or no byte advantage.
not_established_gate: Direct ICL or oracle-FV target accuracy is at/below chance; routing accuracy alone cannot establish useful functional routing.
boundaries: Synthetic GPT-2 task only; not natural-language or causal-head Function Vector evidence.
Task combinations and address count are not capacity claims.
MA-518 factorized decoder defect is not reused; this protocol tests content routing as a distinct degree of freedom.
